author: Athanasius of Alexandria
occasion: Athanasius responds to writings Maximus has sent. He praises Maximus's piety but notes the rashness of those who do not understand what they say, and he dictates a concise response based on what Maximus wrote so that the opponent may be persuaded to cease his evil speaking.
argument: Athanasius opens by explaining his reluctance to answer shameless opponents, citing Jesus's silence before Pilate and Caiaphas, but says Maximus's zeal for the truth moved him to dictate a reply. He argues that the crucified Christ is not a holy man into whom the Word came, but God the Word himself who became flesh once for all from the Virgin Mary for our salvation. He insists that Christ's bodily experiences are real, against the Manichaean phantasm, while his divine works reveal his deity, against the teaching of Paul of Samosata. He concludes by urging adherence to the Nicene confession as sufficient to overturn every heresy, especially the Arian.

outline.move: Athanasius greets Maximus, explains his initial reluctance to answer shameless opponents, and sets out to dictate nothing more than what Maximus wrote, so that the opponent may be persuaded to cease his evil speaking.

Athanasius argues that Christ was not born by natural necessity, that his bodily sufferings and divine works must both be confessed, and that the Nicene faith is sufficient against every heresy, especially the Arian.

cast.name: Athanasius
cast.who: Archbishop of Alexandria and author of the letter.

cast.name: Maximus
cast.who: The philosopher to whom the letter is addressed, praised for his zeal for the truth.

cast.name: Pilate
cast.who: The Roman governor before whom Jesus remained silent.

cast.name: Caiaphas
cast.who: The high priest whose foolish speech Jesus did not answer.

cast.name: Thomas
cast.who: The apostle who touched the crucified Jesus and confessed him as Lord and God.

cast.name: Mary
cast.who: The Virgin from whom the Word came forth as man.

cast.name: Lazarus
cast.who: The dead man whose tomb Jesus asked about in human fashion and raised in divine power.

cast.name: Adam
cast.who: The first man, in whom the sentence of death was spoken to all.

cast.name: Paul of Samosata
cast.who: The heretic who taught that Christ was a mere man distinct from God the Word.

voices.speaker: Jesus
voices.how_marked: Introduced by a participial construction: 'the one saying after washing the disciples' feet' (τὸν μετὰ τὸ νίψαι τοὺς πόδας τῶν μαθητῶν λέγοντα).

voices.speaker: Thomas
voices.how_marked: Introduced by the participle λέγοντα ('the one saying'), with the confession given as indirect statement using the infinitive (αὐτὸν εἶναι).

voices.speaker: The opponents
voices.how_marked: Introduced by the phrase τὸ λέγον ('the saying which says'), followed by a relative clause.

voices.speaker: Scripture (Genesis)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by κατὰ τό... ἐν τῷ Ἀδὰμ εἰρημένον πρὸς πάντας ('according to what was said to Adam and to all').

key_terms.sense: The divine Word of God, the Son, who became flesh for our salvation.
Flesh, the full human bodily nature the Word took from the Virgin.
The cross of Christ, the central scandal for Jews and folly for Greeks.
Man or human being; the opponents wrongly say the Word came into a holy man.
God; Athanasius insists the crucified one is true God, not a mere creature.
The Virgin Mary, whose virginal conception shows Christ's birth was not by natural necessity.
Nature; the opponents claim Christ became man by natural sequence, which Athanasius denies.
Salvation, the purpose for which the Word became man and offered his own body.
Heresy, especially the Arian teaching that blasphemes the Word and the Holy Spirit.
Nicaea, the council whose confession is upheld as sufficient against heresy.

scripture: The author uses Septuagint book names and Psalm numbering. Cite them in modern form, e.g. LXX Psalms as in standard English Bibles, and note LXX/Vulgate numbering where it differs from the Hebrew.
uncertain: The exact date of the letter is not stated in the source.
The precise identity of the opponents is not named; they are described only as those who deny the divinity of the crucified Christ.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ ὁ Σαμοσατεὺς πρόφασιν εὕρῃ
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source form is "Σαμοσατεύς" (nominative singular), not a generic label. The brief correctly identifies this refers to Paul of Samosata, but the source form should be noted as the epithet/nickname form used in the text.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Thomas ... how_marked: 'Introduced by the participle λέγοντα ('the one saying'), with the confession given as indirect statement using the infinitive (αὐτὸν εἶναι).'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: αἰδείσθωσαν τὸν Θωμᾶν τὸν ψηλαφήσαντα τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον, καὶ λέγοντα Κύριον αὐτὸν εἶναι καὶ Θεόν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Thomas is introduced by the article τὸν with two participles in parallel: τὸν ψηλαφήσαντα... καὶ λέγοντα. The confession is a direct statement in indirect discourse (accusative + infinitive), but the marking is through the participles describing Thomas, not solely λέγοντα. More precisely: 'Introduced by the article τὸν with participles ψηλαφήσαντα and λέγοντα, with the confession as accusative-and-infinitive indirect statement.'

_unresolved_facts.claim: The opponents ... how_marked: 'Introduced by the phrase τὸ λέγον ('the saying which says'), followed by a relative clause.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: οὐδὲ καλὸν ἐκεῖνο αὐτῶν τόλμημα τὸ λέγον, ὅτι εἰς ἄνθρωπόν τινα ἅγιον ἐγένετο ὁ τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγος
_unresolved_facts.fix: The opponents are introduced by αὐτῶν ('their') as a genitive of possession with τόλμημα ('daring attempt'), not by τὸ λέγον alone. The phrase is 'ἐκεῖνο αὐτῶν τόλμημα τὸ λέγον' ('that daring attempt of theirs which says'). The how_marked should be: 'Introduced as αὐτῶν τόλμημα τὸ λέγον, a genitive of possession with a substantized participle, followed by ὅτι introducing the content of their claim.'

Jesus speaks in section 2 as well: 'Ὑμεῖς φωνεῖτέ με ὁ Κύριος καὶ ὁ διδάσκαλος, καὶ καλῶς λέγετε· εἰμὶ γάρ.' (though this is in section 1). Additionally, Jesus's words to the Jews are cited in section 1: 'Τί ζητεῖτέ με ἀποκτεῖναι ἄνθρωπον, ὃς τὴν ἀλήθειαν ὑμῖν λελάληκα;' The sections field should be ["1"] but the how_marked is incomplete—Jesus is also introduced by ὡς καὶ πρὸς Ἰουδαίους ἔφη for the second quotation.
